Judge Rita Lin of the US District Court for the Northern District of California issued the ruling on Thursday in a 59-page order.
She found that the Pentagon’s decision to designate Anthropic a “
Lin said the government had retaliated against Anthropic after the company opposed the use of its Claude AI models for certain military purposes.
The empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics,”

The case began after Anthropic refused to allow Claude to support mass surveillance of Americans or autonomous lethal weapons. The Pentagon argued that a private company should not dictate how the US military uses its technology.
The disagreement escalated in February when Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk. The move prevented military contractors from doing business with the company.
The designation marked the first public use of the status against a US company. The government had previously used it against foreign firms considered a threat to military systems.
Anthropic challenged the decision in court, arguing that the Pentagon had violated its First Amendment rights by punishing it for expressing views about AI safety.
It also argued that the government denied it due process by giving it no opportunity to challenge the designation.
The Justice Department rejected those claims. It said the dispute centred on Anthropic’s refusal to accept contractual terms, rather than the company’s views on AI safety.
The government also warned that restrictions on Claude could create uncertainty for the Pentagon. It argued that such uncertainty could affect military systems during operations.
Judge Lin, however, found that the administration’s national security arguments did not justify the action against Anthropic.
She also said the government had moved away from several earlier claims that Anthropic could compromise or disable its technology.
Lin concluded that the decision was driven by a desire to punish Anthropic publicly for criticising the government.

We welcome the court’s ruling that this supply chain risk designation was unlawful. We remain focused on working productively with the government to harness A.I. for our national security so all Americans benefit from this technology.”
The ruling makes permanent an earlier temporary suspension of the sanctions and takes effect immediately. The Trump administration can still appeal the decision.

over a $200 million contract for AI technology on classified military systems.
Anthropic had placed limits on how the military could use Claude. In particular, it opposed domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons.
The Pentagon maintained that those restrictions were unacceptable for military use.
Anthropic has also filed a separate case in Washington, DC, challenging another Pentagon supply-chain risk designation.
If the designation stands, it could affect the company’s ability to secure civilian government contracts.
